newsitem.title: UK: Commercial Union up on merger talk, charts.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union up on merger talk, charts.

text.p: Shares in Commercial Union Plc rose on the back of fresh speculation about a possible merger with the insurance operations of another British company and on a technical bounce after recent declines, traders said.

The Daily Mail reported that expectations were rising for B.A.T. Industries to demerge its financial arm, which would then merge with Commerical Union. Advisers confirmed that contacts took place this year but a deal foundered, it reported.
But traders downplayed the report, saying it was nothing new and share prices would be marked up substantially more if it proved to be true.
By 0927 GMT, Commercial Union shares were up 8-1/2p at 640p after reaching a high of 647p. B.A.T. was up 9-1/2p at 547p.
"It's a technical bounce, it's oversold," one trader said. "If there was going to be any more talk (about merging) it would be up more than this."
Traders said a B.A.T demerger could be more likely after a U.S. tobacco litigation settlement earlier this month.
A Commercial Union spokesman declined comment. B.A.T. Industries was not immediately available for comment.
